title: Patient outcomes data analysis and reporting
problem: CNSs spend significant time manually collecting, analyzing, and reporting nurse-sensitive indicators (NDNQI, HCAHPS) to demonstrate quality improvement. Calculating rates for falls, pressure injuries, CAUTI, CLABSI across units requires pulling data from multiple EHR sources and performing statistical analysis. Errors in calculation can misrepresent unit performance and lead to incorrect QI interventions.
who: Hospital-based CNSs responsible for quality improvement reporting

skill_spec.name: Nurse-Sensitive Indicator Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates nurse-sensitive quality indicators (fall rates, infection rates, pressure injury prevalence) per 1,000 patient days with benchmarking

inputs.name: indicator_type
inputs.label: Indicator type (falls, CAUTI, CLABSI, pressure injury, restraint use)

inputs.name: event_count
inputs.label: Number of events in reporting period

inputs.name: patient_days
inputs.label: Total patient days in reporting period

skill_spec.formula_hint: Rate = (event_count / patient_days) * 1000; for device-associated = (event_count / device_days) * 1000; compare against NDNQI benchmark tables by unit type

example_queries: We had 7 patient falls on a 30-bed med-surg unit with 840 patient days last month. What's our fall rate and how does it compare to the national benchmark?
Calculate our CAUTI rate: 3 infections, 1,200 catheter days in the ICU
What's the pressure injury prevalence rate if we found 12 cases during a survey of 200 patients?

title: CNS role ROI calculation for administrators
problem: CNSs struggle to demonstrate their financial value to hospital administrators, especially during budget cuts. They need to quantify cost savings from reduced complications, shorter lengths of stay, decreased readmissions, and staff turnover reduction. Without clear ROI data, CNS positions are often the first eliminated during cost-cutting, despite generating significant savings.
who: All CNSs, especially those in organizations questioning CNS value

skill_spec.name: CNS Role ROI Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates the financial return on investment of a CNS position by quantifying cost avoidance from prevented complications, reduced LOS, and decreased turnover

inputs.name: los_reduction_days
inputs.label: Total LOS days reduced across patients

inputs.name: nurses_retained
inputs.label: Nurses retained (who would have left without CNS mentoring)

skill_spec.formula_hint: Fall with injury cost ~$14,000; CAUTI ~$13,000; CLABSI ~$48,000; pressure injury ~$26,000; daily hospital bed cost ~$2,500; readmission penalty ~$15,000; RN turnover cost ~$56,000; ROI = (total_savings - cns_cost) / cns_cost * 100

example_queries: I make $130,000 with benefits. This year I prevented an estimated 10 falls, 4 CAUTIs, and reduced LOS by 50 days total. What's my ROI?
Help me build a business case for keeping my CNS position - our unit reduced CLABSIs from 8 to 2 this year and retained 3 nurses who were planning to leave
Calculate ROI for a CNS earning $140K who prevented 15 pressure injuries and 6 readmissions

title: Staff competency assessment tracking
problem: CNSs are responsible for developing and tracking competency assessments for nursing staff across multiple units. Managing who has been assessed, what competencies are due, tracking expiration dates, and ensuring compliance with Joint Commission requirements involves extensive spreadsheet management. Missed competency validations can result in accreditation citations.
who: CNSs responsible for staff education and competency validation

skill_spec.name: Staff Competency Assessment Tracker
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates a competency validation checklist with regulatory requirements, assessment methods, and documentation standards per Joint Commission and specialty requirements
steps: Step 1: Identify competency domain (clinical skill, equipment, medication, population-specific)
Step 2: Determine regulatory requirement source (Joint Commission HR.01.06.01, state BON, specialty standard)
Step 3: Define competency criteria and performance expectations
Step 4: Select assessment method (direct observation, simulation, written test, case study, peer review)
Step 5: Create competency assessment tool with measurable criteria
Step 6: Schedule initial and ongoing assessment intervals (annual, biannual, or trigger-based)
Step 7: Document assessment results with date, assessor, score, and remediation plan if needed
Step 8: Track completion rates by unit and identify overdue assessments
Step 9: File documentation in employee competency record
Step 10: Report aggregate compliance data to nursing leadership
warnings: Warning: Joint Commission requires competency assessment at hire and ongoing - not just annual
Warning: High-risk/low-volume competencies require more frequent validation
Warning: Agency/travel nurses require competency verification before patient care assignment
Warning: Competency assessment must match actual job responsibilities, not generic checklists

example_queries: What competencies do I need to validate for new ICU nurses per Joint Commission standards?
Create a competency assessment checklist for chemotherapy administration
What are the required steps to document a competency validation for blood product administration?

title: Evidence-based practice guideline development
problem: CNSs spend 26.5% of their time on evidence-based practice projects but struggle with the systematic process of translating research into clinical protocols. The process from literature search to policy implementation involves multiple steps that are easy to skip or do out of order, risking adoption of weak evidence or failure to get organizational buy-in.
who: CNSs leading EBP projects and practice change initiatives

skill_spec.name: EBP Project Implementation Checklist
skill_spec.one_liner: Step-by-step guide for implementing an evidence-based practice change using the Iowa Model or Johns Hopkins EBP framework
steps: Step 1: Identify clinical problem using PICOT format (Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome, Time)
Step 2: Form interprofessional EBP team with stakeholder representation
Step 3: Conduct systematic literature search (PubMed, CINAHL, Cochrane, UpToDate)
Step 4: Critically appraise evidence using hierarchy of evidence (Level I-VII)
Step 5: Synthesize evidence and determine strength of recommendation
Step 6: Develop clinical protocol/guideline draft based on evidence synthesis
Step 7: Obtain organizational approvals (nursing practice council, medical staff, compliance)
Step 8: Design pilot implementation plan with measurable outcomes
Step 9: Implement pilot on selected unit(s) with staff education
Step 10: Collect and analyze outcome data using PDSA cycle
Step 11: Revise protocol based on pilot results
Step 12: Scale to organization-wide implementation
Step 13: Develop sustainability plan with auditing schedule
Step 14: Disseminate results (poster, presentation, publication)
warnings: Warning: Do not skip critical appraisal - weak evidence leads to harmful practice changes
Warning: Stakeholder buy-in before pilot prevents implementation failure
Warning: IRB review may be required if outcomes will be published as research
Warning: Allow minimum 3-month pilot period for meaningful outcome measurement

example_queries: Walk me through implementing an EBP project to reduce CAUTI rates using the Iowa Model
I want to change our fall prevention protocol based on new evidence - what steps do I need to follow?
How do I critically appraise the evidence for early mobility in the ICU and build a protocol?

title: Joint Commission accreditation survey preparation
problem: Accreditation surveys create peak preparation periods requiring CNSs to ensure all clinical protocols, competency records, and quality data are survey-ready. Missing or outdated documentation can result in citations, conditional accreditation, or loss of accreditation - directly threatening hospital CMS reimbursement. CNSs must coordinate across multiple departments under tight deadlines.
who: CNSs involved in accreditation preparation at hospitals and health systems

skill_spec.name: Joint Commission Survey Readiness Checklist
skill_spec.one_liner: Comprehensive checklist for CNS-led Joint Commission survey preparation covering nursing-specific standards, documentation, and tracer readiness
steps: Step 1: Review current Joint Commission National Patient Safety Goals (NPSGs) and verify unit compliance
Step 2: Audit clinical protocols and policies for currency (updated within required timeframe)
Step 3: Verify staff competency files are complete (HR.01.06.01) - all staff, including agency
Step 4: Review quality metrics and ensure data collection methodology is documented
Step 5: Conduct mock tracer activities: individual patient tracer, system tracer, program-specific tracer
Step 6: Verify medication management compliance (MM chapter) - labeling, storage, high-alert meds
Step 7: Audit infection prevention practices (IC chapter) - hand hygiene, isolation, device bundles
Step 8: Review restraint usage documentation and policies (PC.03.05.01-PC.03.05.19)
Step 9: Verify pain assessment and management documentation compliance
Step 10: Ensure fall prevention program documentation is current with outcome data
Step 11: Review nursing documentation for completeness in EHR (assessments, care plans, education)
Step 12: Prepare staff for surveyor interviews - key talking points for bedside nurses
Step 13: Verify emergency equipment checks are documented and current
Step 14: Compile evidence binder/digital folder with QI data, EBP projects, and outcomes
warnings: Warning: Joint Commission surveys are unannounced - maintain continuous readiness
Warning: Loss of accreditation can terminate CMS reimbursement
Warning: Surveyors interview frontline staff - preparation must extend beyond leadership
Warning: Documentation gaps are the #1 citation category

example_queries: What nursing-specific areas do I need to prepare for a Joint Commission survey?
Give me a checklist for conducting mock tracer activities on my unit
What are the most common Joint Commission citations CNSs should watch for?

title: Clinical protocol and policy document generation
problem: CNSs regularly write and update clinical protocols, policies, and practice guidelines. Each document requires a standardized format including purpose, scope, definitions, procedure steps, evidence references, approval signatures, and review dates. Writing these from scratch is time-consuming and inconsistency in format can cause confusion and compliance issues.
who: CNSs responsible for developing and maintaining clinical policies and protocols

skill_spec.name: Clinical Protocol Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates standardized clinical protocol/policy documents with evidence-based content, regulatory references, and proper organizational formatting

variables.name: clinical_area
variables.label: Clinical area (ICU, Med-Surg, OR, ED, etc.)

skill_spec.structure_hint: Header (title, number, dates) -> Purpose -> Scope -> Definitions -> Policy Statement -> Procedure (numbered steps) -> Evidence/References -> Related Policies -> Approval Signatures -> Review History

example_queries: Generate a clinical protocol template for central line dressing change in the ICU
Create a nursing policy document for early mobility in mechanically ventilated patients
Write a protocol for nurse-driven urinary catheter removal based on current evidence

title: Quality improvement project report generation
problem: CNSs must regularly produce QI reports documenting project progress, outcome data, statistical analysis, and recommendations for leadership. These reports must follow specific formats expected by quality committees, Magnet documentation, and accreditation bodies. Creating these reports from scratch each time is repetitive and delays project advancement.

skill_spec.name: QI Project Report Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates structured quality improvement project reports using PDSA framework with data visualization guidance and executive summary
skill_spec.structure_hint: Executive Summary -> Background/Problem Statement -> SMART Aim -> Team Members -> Methodology (PDSA) -> Intervention Description -> Data Collection Methods -> Results (with run chart/control chart guidance) -> Analysis -> Lessons Learned -> Next Steps -> Appendices

example_queries: Generate a QI report for our CAUTI reduction project - baseline was 3.2/1000 catheter days, now 1.1 after 6 months
Create a PDSA cycle report template for our fall prevention initiative
Write up our QI results on reducing hospital-acquired pressure injuries for the quality committee

title: APRN scope of practice by state lookup
problem: CNS scope of practice varies dramatically by state - 28 states plus DC have full practice authority, while others require physician collaboration or supervision. Prescriptive authority laws are actively changing (Maryland 2025 allows CNS prescribing). CNSs moving between states, consulting across state lines, or advocating for legislative changes need quick, accurate reference to current state-specific regulations.
who: All CNSs, especially those in multi-state practice, telehealth, or legislative advocacy

skill_spec.name: CNS Scope of Practice State Reference
skill_spec.one_liner: Quick lookup of CNS/APRN scope of practice, prescriptive authority, and collaboration requirements by state with recent legislative changes
skill_spec.data_domain: State-by-state APRN/CNS scope of practice regulations, prescriptive authority, and practice authority classifications

data_hints.source_law: State Nurse Practice Acts, APRN Consensus Model
data_hints.recent_changes: Maryland 2025 CNS prescribing authority, Wisconsin full practice authority bill pending
data_hints.categories: Full Practice (28 states + DC), Reduced Practice, Restricted Practice

example_queries: Can a CNS prescribe medications in Maryland under the new 2025 law?
Which states have full practice authority for APRNs and what does that mean for CNS practice?
I'm a CNS in Texas considering a move to California - how does scope of practice differ?

title: CNS certification and license renewal requirements
problem: CNSs must maintain multiple credentials - state nursing license, APRN license, national certification (ANCC or specialty board), and continuing education requirements. Each has different renewal cycles, CE requirements, and documentation standards. Missing a renewal deadline can result in inability to practice, loss of prescriptive authority, and employment termination.
who: All practicing CNSs managing multiple certifications and licenses

skill_spec.name: CNS Credential Renewal Reference
skill_spec.one_liner: Reference guide for CNS certification renewal requirements including CE hours, practice hours, and deadlines by certifying body
skill_spec.data_domain: APRN/CNS certification and license renewal requirements by certifying body and state

data_hints.source_law: ANCC Certification Requirements, State Nurse Practice Acts
data_hints.common_requirements: 75 CE hours/5 years for ANCC, 1000 practice hours, pharmacology CE for prescribers

example_queries: What are the ANCC renewal requirements for my Adult-Gerontology CNS certification?
How many CE hours do I need for CNS certification renewal and how many must be pharmacology?
My ANCC certification expires in 6 months - what do I need to have completed?

title: Staff education program development
problem: CNSs spend 26.5% of their day teaching nurses and staff but creating education materials from scratch for each topic is time-consuming. Education programs must include learning objectives, content aligned with evidence, competency evaluation methods, and documentation for accreditation. Poorly designed education leads to knowledge gaps and patient safety issues.
who: CNSs responsible for nursing staff education and professional development

skill_spec.name: Nursing Education Program Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates structured nursing education program outlines with learning objectives, evidence-based content, teaching strategies, and competency evaluation plans

variables.name: target_audience
variables.label: Target audience (new grads, experienced RNs, all staff)

skill_spec.structure_hint: Title/Date -> Needs Assessment Justification -> Learning Objectives (SMART) -> Content Outline -> Teaching Strategies -> Materials Needed -> Competency Evaluation Method -> Documentation Requirements -> Post-Education Follow-up Plan

example_queries: Create an education program on sepsis early recognition for med-surg nurses
Design a simulation-based education plan for rapid response team activation
Generate a staff education outline for new insulin pump protocol implementation

title: Medication dosage and drip rate calculations
problem: CNSs frequently need to verify complex medication calculations including weight-based dosing, drip rates, titration parameters, and pediatric/neonatal dosing. While pharmacists are available, CNSs need rapid independent verification during clinical consultations, simulation teaching, and when developing medication protocols. Errors in dosage calculations are a leading cause of preventable patient harm.
who: CNSs with prescriptive authority and those developing medication protocols

skill_spec.name: Clinical Dosage Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates weight-based medication dosages, IV drip rates, and titration parameters with safety range verification
skill_spec.formula_hint: Weight-based: dose = ordered_dose * weight; Drip rate (mL/hr) = (dose_per_min * 60 * volume) / drug_amount; gtts/min = (volume * drop_factor) / (time_min); verify against safe dose range

example_queries: Calculate dopamine drip rate: ordered 5 mcg/kg/min, patient weighs 80kg, concentration is 400mg in 250mL D5W
What's the correct dose of vancomycin 15mg/kg for a 92kg patient and what's the infusion rate?
Verify this heparin calculation: 18 units/kg/hr for a 70kg patient, concentration 25,000 units in 500mL

title: Root cause analysis facilitation
problem: When sentinel events or near-misses occur, CNSs are often tasked with leading root cause analysis (RCA). The RCA process is complex, requiring systematic investigation, fishbone diagrams, contributing factor identification, and corrective action plans. Incomplete RCAs lead to recurring events and potential Joint Commission citations. CNSs need guidance on proper methodology and documentation.
who: CNSs involved in patient safety and quality management

skill_spec.name: Root Cause Analysis Advisor
skill_spec.one_liner: Guides CNSs through conducting root cause analysis for patient safety events with structured methodology, contributing factor identification, and corrective action planning
skill_spec.expertise_area: Patient safety event investigation and root cause analysis methodology
decision_criteria: event type (sentinel, adverse, near-miss, hazardous condition)

example_queries: A patient fell and fractured their hip despite being on fall precautions. Walk me through conducting the RCA.
How do I structure a fishbone diagram for a medication error involving wrong-dose administration?
What corrective actions should I recommend after our RCA found communication failures during a rapid response?

title: Navigating role ambiguity and organizational positioning
problem: CNS role ambiguity is the top career fear - many CNSs are seen as overhead rather than essential. They struggle to articulate their unique value compared to NPs, nurse educators, and quality coordinators. Without clear role definition and strategic positioning, CNSs face job elimination during budget cuts and lack career advancement pathways.
who: New and experienced CNSs facing role ambiguity or organizational restructuring

skill_spec.name: CNS Role Strategy Advisor
skill_spec.one_liner: Advises CNSs on defining, communicating, and protecting their organizational role using the three spheres of influence framework and outcome metrics
skill_spec.expertise_area: CNS role definition, organizational positioning, and career strategy within healthcare systems

example_queries: My hospital is considering eliminating my CNS position to hire another NP. How do I make the case to keep my role?
How do I explain the difference between a CNS and a nurse educator to my nursing director?
I feel like I'm being used as a staff nurse rather than functioning in my CNS role. How do I reset expectations with my manager?
